context: A grandmother teaches her granddaughter about kindness and old shop signs
purpose: Teach: 寿司/麺/花火/親切/暗い/天井/払う/終わら

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: ほら、あの看板見える?天井のすぐ下に掛かってる、昔ながらの寿司屋さんのよ。
lines.en: See that sign? Hanging just below the ceiling—it's from an old sushi shop.
lines.style: Warm grandmother pointing up gently, sharing local history

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: へえ、ちょっと暗いから読めないなあ。私、ラーメン屋さんの麺の絵かと思ってた。
lines.en: Huh, it's so dark I can't read it. I thought it was a ramen shop's noodle picture.
lines.style: Curious teen squinting upward with a playful, casual tone

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: むかしね、夏の花火の夜に、お代を払うのを忘れて帰っちゃったお客さんがいたのよ。
lines.en: Long ago, on a summer fireworks night, a customer went home forgetting to pay.
lines.style: Storytelling grandmother sharing a fond memory with warmth

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: えっ、お店の人、怒らなかったの?
lines.en: What? The shop owner didn't get angry?
lines.style: Surprised teenager leaning in eagerly to hear more

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: それがね、とても親切な方で、「いつでもいいよ」って笑って許してくれたんですって。
lines.en: Well, he was such a kind man—he laughed and said, 'Anytime is fine.'
lines.style: Gentle voice recalling a tender act of generosity warmly

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: いい話だね。そういう温かい話、いつまで聞いても終わらないでほしいな。
lines.en: What a lovely story. I wish warm tales like that would never end.
lines.style: Touched teen speaking softly with genuine admiration and wonder

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: そうね。看板は古びても、人の親切は消えないものなのよ、さくら。
lines.en: Indeed. Signs may fade with age, but human kindness never disappears, Sakura.
lines.style: Sage, loving grandmother imparting a quiet life lesson softly
